# Craft floor

Load this after the direction is settled, within the current controller's authorized scope. The accepted brief and target world govern. These checks are design knowledge for actual evidence, not tool grants, model rules or a second style authority.

## Verify

Each of these is a check on the built result, not an intention. Run them together in the batched inspection rounds, not as separate screenshot trips; the checks share one render.

- **Contrast:** measure actual normal/large text and meaningful non-text roles, states and themes against the accepted criterion and applicable exceptions. A chosen color recipe alone proves nothing.
- **Depth:** elevation and material must carry the chosen hierarchy/state; preserve an intentional accepted flat, halo, shadow or outlined language when it serves the task.
- **Spacing:** group related content and separate distinct groups; compare computed and rendered rhythm rather than impose a new base over target tokens.
- **Type:** use the actual face, role, language, viewport and user scaling; measure/readability ranges are starting points, not universal size/tracking gates.
- **Motion:** purposeful, visible by default, interruptible and reduced-motion aware; a focal sequence is optional and must not delay the task.
- **States:** required default/hover/focus/disabled/loading/error/empty/success/permission behavior, real content and working controls at required sizes.
- **Platform surfaces:** respect browser/native user settings and accepted target conventions; theme incidental chrome only when it improves the task without defeating platform accessibility.
- **Copy:** the product's own language. Controls name their action; errors name the problem and the recovery. 
- **Coverage:** every brief requirement present and findable within seconds. 

## Design risks to assess in context

These are useful prompts, not bans. An accepted brief, coherent incumbent system or a specific task reason can justify each pattern. Judge whether it serves content, hierarchy, state, platform and user outcome rather than refuse it by name.

Page structure:

- Repeated equal cards can flatten unlike information; nested containers can add noise. Use cards when the grouped objects are genuinely comparable or actionable.
- A large metric may dominate without explaining its meaning; keep it truthful and provide needed context.
- Kickers/eyebrows and section numbers should add real category/sequence meaning rather than restate a heading.
- A modal should earn protected focus or interruption; inline interaction may be simpler when recovery is safe.

Surface and material:

- Gradients, glass, glows, side stripes, hard shadows, sparklines and progress rings need a semantic/material role in the accepted direction, not a default decoration layer.
- Monospace, system fonts, handwritten lettering and display faces are valid when they fit actual content, platform, reading and brand. No external typeface acquisition is implied.
- Keep a coherent icon system with meaningful accessible names; glyphs/emoji can be content but should not obscure control meaning or platform expectations.
- Organic cutouts should retain their actual silhouette if that promise matters; alpha/image assets and precise vectors are options under actual available tools/rights.
- A theme follows accepted brand and the usage scene, not category habit alone. Any illustration, texture, grid or shader must earn its place and fit the budget.

Examples for review:

- Optical tracking, radius and elevation vary by face/role/component; preserve accepted values before inventing a new scale.
- Illustration can be raster, crisp vector, diagram or generated material as appropriate; provenance and truthful presentation matter more than a model-specific style ban.
- Repeating lines/grids and distressed material need a real visual/content purpose; avoid a costume that fights comprehension.
- Claims and configuration come from accepted truth. Clearly labeled illustrative material stays separate from actual outcomes/capabilities.

No reference taste rule can override an accepted comp/brief or certify the build.

The floor holds the mechanics; it never picks the direction. With every check green, spend the page on the committed world, and when torn between refined and committed, commit.
